title: [SeatMap][Request] Apply the three universal caller-facing security checks (invalid x-api-key, invalid Client-Id, cross-tenant supplier/credentialsSelector) to GetSeatMap.
spec_ref: SPEC.md §7.14; User Story AC8 ("securely authenticates" -- caller-facing half only, see TC-SEATMAP-SEC-02)
request_summary: GetSeatMap on a valid GulfAir/KSA offer (BAH-RUH 2027-06-14): (1) invalid x-api-key, (2) invalid Client-Id, (3a) supplier/selector switched to TravelportNdc/UAE, (3b) same supplier GulfAir with credentialsSelector switched to UAE; extra probes: empty/missing x-api-key, missing Client-Id, bogus selector ZZZ, omitted selector
response_summary: (1) 401 AuthenticationError; (2) 401 AuthenticationError; (3a) 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001; (3b) 200 - the full seat map was returned; extras: empty key 401, missing key 401, missing Client-Id 401, ZZZ 400, omitted selector 400
expected: All three variants rejected (exact status/error shape UNKNOWN; reuse the envelope other endpoints produce)
actual: Two of three checks pass cleanly; the third half-passes. Invalid x-api-key and invalid Client-Id are rejected 401 AuthenticationError (also for empty/missing key and missing Client-Id). A wrong supplier is rejected (400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 'Failed to deserialize the selected offer'). But switching only credentialsSelector to another valid one for the same supplier (GulfAir/UAE) is NOT rejected: GetSeatMap returns the complete seat map, same responseId, for an offer created under KSA. credentialsSelector is still not enforced as an authorization boundary on GetSeatMap (BUG-17, 4th round observed). Bogus/omitted selectors are rejected 400 (different envelope: lowercase keys, errorCode 1001).
evidence: control 200; bad key 401; empty key 401; missing key 401; bad Client-Id 401; missing Client-Id 401; TravelportNdc/UAE 400; GulfAir/UAE 200 (sameResponseId=true, 201301 bytes vs control 203091); ZZZ 400; omitted 400

title: [SeatMap][Documentation] Record that supplier-side authentication security (this API's own credentials presented to the airline/GDS backend) and request/response logging are not independently verifiable through this API's black-box contract, and identify the correct verification channel for each.
spec_ref: SPEC.md §1.5, §1.8; NDC_PRD.md §7, Gap #1; User Story AC8, AC9 (partial)
request_summary: N/A - documentation/scope-boundary case, no live API call
expected: Documented per 1.5/1.8/PRD 7: AC8 (supplier-side authentication) and the logging half of AC9 are confirmable only via a backend credential/config audit and log/observability review, not through this suite; AC9 graceful-error half is covered by TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05
actual: Documented as specified; SPEC.md 1.5 and 1.8 and NDC_PRD.md Gap #1 (hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id) re-checked and still say the same. AC8/AC9 must not be marked covered by API tests without the paired backend/config/log audit. Unchanged from Rounds 1-16.
evidence: No API call made, per the test case definition; SPEC.md headings 1.5/1.8 and PRD Gap #1 line verified present in a separate check

view_tc.steps: Review SPEC.md §1.5/§1.8 (static, hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id sent by THIS layer to the caller; supplier-side credentials are a separate, server-side-only concern not exposed in any request/response this suite can observe) and the PRD's §7 Non-Functional Requirements (file-only ApiResponse/SLF4J logger, correlation-ID tracing) for what actually governs supplier-auth and logging.
view_tc.expected_result: This case does not assert a pass/fail against the live API. It documents that: (a) User Story AC8's "securely authenticates with airline supplier APIs" describes THIS system's outbound credential handling toward suppliers -- a server-side/config concern, confirmable only via a backend credential-storage/config audit or the automation framework's own code review (PRD §7's Gap #1 already flags this as hardcoded tech debt), not via any request this Postman-collection-driven suite can send; (b) AC9's "provides logging" is confirmable only via log/observability review (PRD §7's ApiResponse logger, correlation-ID tracing), not via API response inspection. TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05 covers AC9's "handles errors gracefully" half, which IS API-observable.
view_tc.notes: Do not mark AC8/AC9 as "covered by automated API tests" without pairing this row with the corresponding backend/config/log audit -- that pairing, not this row alone, is what closes those two acceptance criteria.

title: [SeatMap][Request] Validate a cellID obtained from one offer's GetSeatMap response is rejected when submitted in Book for a different offer.
endpoint_or_flow: Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (x2 offers) -> Book
request_summary: Book on offer B (BAH-JED 2027-06-20) with seat cellCode 12D but cellId = the cellID issued for the same seat 12D on a different offer A (BAH-JED 2027-06-19); two independent Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap chains
response_summary: 200 - pnr OVAMWU ticketed (722137003884) after 29.5s; passengersSelectedSeats came back {} and Retrieve confirms no seat, no 120 SAR fee (total 1143 SAR)
expected: Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9), since cellID appears (per its base64-decoded contents) to embed the originating ResponseId/OfferId/passenger-ref metadata and is presumably bound to the offer it was issued for.
actual: Not rejected. Book accepted a cellId bound (per its decoded contents: Offer A responseId cf885a30-bc26-43e4-8449-5c6e95cc055e, segment ...2027061901..., seat 12D) to a different offer, ran the full booking, issued a ticket and silently dropped the seat instead of returning an error. The same cellCode was used on both offers so only the cellId binding differs - the server neither validates it against Offer B nor reports the mismatch. BUG-07 reproduces (12th time).
evidence: Book 200 pnr OVAMWU ticket 722137003884; passengersSelectedSeats {}; Retrieve passengersSelectedSeats {}; cellID_A decoded: [GF $cfaf69e6-ea23-4b28-8db5-1877e8ab6970 &GF-GF181-GF181-2027061901-2027061904-O PAX1 GF-SeatOffer1 &GF-GF181-GF181-2027061901-2027061904-O 120.00 SAR BAH JED l D 12D $cf885a30-bc26-43e4-8449-5c6e95cc055e]; cellID_B decoded: [GF $4c8f94b8-7c51-45dd-b5c7-eaaddc2706fb &GF-GF181-GF181-2027062001-2027062004-O PAX1 GF-SeatOffer1 &GF-GF181-GF181-2027062001-2027062004-O 120.00 SAR BAH JED l ! 12D $fffbc381-c431-4e1c-acb7-4cf85e829dae]; cellID_A != cellID_B (true)

hops.request_summary: Book on Offer B with seat cellCode 12D but cellId = cellID_A (issued for Offer A)

view_tc.preconditions: Two independent, completed Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chains (Offer A and Offer B) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
view_tc.steps: Chain A: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, record cellID_A. Chain B: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, obtain getSeatMapResponceID_B/getSeatMapOfferId_B. Book using Chain B's ResponseId/selectedOfferId but passengersSelectedSeats.cellId=cellID_A.
view_tc.expected_result: Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9), since cellID appears (per its base64-decoded contents) to embed the originating ResponseId/OfferId/passenger-ref metadata and is presumably bound to the offer it was issued for.
view_tc.notes: High-value negative test derived directly from the observed structure of the cellID token (SPEC.md §2.7's decoded-metadata observation) -- do not skip on the assumption the token is unchecked server-side.

summary: GetSeatMap does not reject a request whose credentialsSelector differs from the one the offer was created under (same supplier, different valid selector).
expected_value: 4xx rejection (offer not found / not authorized for this credentialsSelector), as happens when the supplier is switched
impact: credentialsSelector is the per-tenant boundary; a caller holding an offerId/responseId from one tenant (KSA) can read that offer's seat map through another tenant's selector (UAE), so cross-tenant isolation rests only on offer IDs being unguessable. Other offer-consuming endpoints were not tested.
